5201.subject: Chemistry
5201.text: A $25 \%$ solution of cane-sugar (molar mass $=342 \mathrm{ g} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$ ) is isotonic with $5 \%$ solution of a substance $A$. Then find the molecular weight of $A$.
5201.sol:
Two solutions are isotonic when they have the same osmotic pressure. It is only possible when they have same molar concentration.
A $25 \%$ solution of cane-sugar means $100 \mathrm{ g}$ of solution contain $25 \mathrm{ g}$ of cane-sugar.
For dilute solution $100 \mathrm{ g}$ is approximately equal to $100 \mathrm{ mL}$.
Molarity of cane-sugar $\begin{aligned}& =\frac{\text{ Number of mole of cane-sugar }}{\text{ Volume (in L) }}\\
& =\frac{25 \mathrm{ g}}{342 \mathrm{ g} / \mathrm{mol} \times 100 \mathrm{ mL}} \times1000 \mathrm{ mL}\\
& =0.7309 \mathrm{M}...( i)
\end{aligned} Now, 5 \%$ solution of substance A$ means 100 \mathrm{ g}$ of the solution contain $5 \mathrm{ g}$ of substance A$.
For dilute solution, 100 \mathrm{ g}$ is approximately equal to $100 \mathrm{ mL}$
Molarity o $\text{$ of $} \begin{aligned} A & =\frac{5 \mathrm{ g}}{M^{\prime} \mathrm{g} / \mathrm{mol} \times 100 \mathrm{ mL}} \times1000 \mathrm{ mL}\\
& =\frac{50}{M^{\prime}} \mathrm{M}...( ii)
\end{aligned} Equating both equations (i) and (ii), we get \begin{aligned}\frac{50}{M^{\prime}}& =0.7309 \\
M^{\prime} & =\frac{50}{0.7309}\\
& =68.408 \mathrm{ g} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$ Hence, molecular weight of A$ is 68.4 \mathrm{ g} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$.

6168.text: The point on the curve $y=x^2+4 x+3$ which is closest to the line $y=3 x+2$ is
6168.sol:
Let $(x, y)$ be on the parabola $y=x^2+4 x+3$
which is closet to the line $y=3 x+2$
Perpendicular distance between a point $\left(x_1, y_1\right)$
and a line $(a x+b y+c=0)D=\left|\frac{a x_1+b y_1+c}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}\right|\left[\therefore\right.$ line $3 x-y+2=0$ at point $\left.\left(x_1, y_1\right)\right]D=\left|\frac{3 x-y+2}{\sqrt{(3)^2+(-1)^2}}\right|=\frac{\left|3 x-\left(x^2+4 x+3\right)+2\right|}{\sqrt{9+1}}\Rightarrow \quad D=\frac{\left|-x^2-x-1\right|}{\sqrt{10}}\Rightarrow \quad D=\frac{x^2+x+1}{\sqrt{10}}=\frac{\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+\frac{3}{4}}{\sqrt{10}}$
On differentiating w.r.t. $x$,
$\frac{d D}{d x}=\frac{\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2}{\sqrt{10}}+\frac{\frac{3}{4}}{\sqrt{10}}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{d D}{d x}=0, x=\frac{-1}{2} \Rightarrow y=x^2+4 x+3 \\ & \Rightarrow y=\left(\frac{-1}{2}\right)^2+(4)\left(\frac{-1}{2}\right)+3 \Rightarrow y=\frac{1}{4}+3-2=0 \\ & \Rightarrow y=\frac{1+12-8}{4} \Rightarrow y=\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}\frac{d D}{d x}=\frac{2\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)}{\sqrt{10}} \Rightarrow \frac{d^2 D}{d x^2} \gt 0$
Hence, minimum at $\left(\frac{-1}{2}, \frac{5}{4}\right)$.

11091.text: In $∆ ABC, A = 75 ° , B = 45 °$ then the value of $b + c\sqrt{2} =$
11091.sol:
Given in $∆ ABC, A = 75 ° , B = 45 °$

$⇒ C = 180 ° - 75 ° - 45 ° = 60 °$ (Using Angle Sum property of triangle)

Also, $sin75 ° = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{2\sqrt{2}}$, $sin45 ° = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $sin60 ° = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

Now, using Sine rule, $\dfrac{a}{sinA} = \dfrac{b}{sinB} = \dfrac{c}{sinC}$

$⇒ \dfrac{a}{\dfrac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{2\sqrt{2}}} = \dfrac{b}{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}} = \dfrac{c}{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(2\sqrt{2}\right)a}{\sqrt{3} + 1} = \sqrt{2}b = \dfrac{2c}{\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ b = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}a}{\sqrt{2}\left(\sqrt{3} + 1\right)} = \dfrac{2a}{\sqrt{3} + 1}$

and $c = \dfrac{\left(2\sqrt{2}\right)a}{\sqrt{3} + 1} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6}a}{\sqrt{3} + 1}$

Now, $L . H . S . = b + c\sqrt{2}$

$= \dfrac{2a}{\sqrt{3} + 1} + \dfrac{\sqrt{6}a}{\sqrt{3} + 1} \times \sqrt{2}$

$= \dfrac{2a + 2\sqrt{3}a}{\sqrt{3} + 1}$

$= \dfrac{2a\left(1 + \sqrt{3}\right)}{\sqrt{3 + 1}} = 2a = R . H . S .$

11592.text: If the roots of the equation $16 x^3-44 x^2+36 x-9=0$ are in harmonic progression, then its greatest root is
11592.sol:
The given equation is
$16 x^3-44 x^2+36 x-9=0$
Let $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ are in H.P.
$\Rightarrow \frac{3}{\beta}=\frac{1}{\alpha}+\frac{1}{\gamma}+\frac{1}{\beta} \Rightarrow \frac{3}{\beta}=\frac{\alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\gamma \alpha}{\alpha \gamma \beta}\Rightarrow \frac{3}{\beta}=\frac{36 / 16}{9 / 16}=4 \Rightarrow \beta=\frac{3}{4}$
Now, $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=\frac{11}{4} \Rightarrow \alpha+\gamma=\frac{11}{4}-\frac{3}{4}=2$...(i)
And $\alpha \beta \gamma=\frac{9}{16} \Rightarrow \alpha \gamma=\frac{9}{16} \times \frac{4}{3}=\frac{3}{4}$...(ii)
Solving eqn. (i) and (ii) :
$\alpha=\frac{3}{2}, \gamma=\frac{1}{2}\therefore$ Greatest root is $\alpha=\frac{3}{2}$.

16151.text: A lens forms real and virtual images of an object when the object is at ${u}_{1}$ and ${u}_{2}$ distances respectively. If the size of the virtual image is double that of the real image, then the focal length of the lens is (Take the magnification of the real image as $' m '$)

The formula of focal length for a convex lens is,

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$, and formula for magnification, $m = \dfrac{v}{u}$.

For real image,

${u}_{1}\left(- ve\right), {v}_{1}\left(+ ve\right) ⇒ \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v1} + \dfrac{1}{u1} ⇒ \dfrac{u1}{f} = \dfrac{u1}{v1} + 1 ⇒ \dfrac{u1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{m} + 1 . . . Eq \left(1\right)$

Similarly, for virtual image case, we can write

${u}_{2}\left(-ve\right), {v}_{2}\left(-ve\right) ⇒ \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{f} = - \dfrac{1}{v2} + \dfrac{1}{u2}$⇒ $\dfrac{u2}{f} = - \dfrac{u2}{v2} +1 ⇒ \dfrac{u2}{f} = \dfrac{1}{- 2m} +1 ⇒ \dfrac{- {u}_{2}}{f} = \dfrac{1}{2m} -1 . . . Eq \left(2\right)$

From both equations, we can write

$\dfrac{{u}_{1} - {u}_{2}}{f} = \dfrac{1}{m} +1 + \dfrac{1}{2m} -1 ⇒ \dfrac{{u}_{1} - {u}_{2}}{f} = \dfrac{3}{2m}⇒ f = \dfrac{2\left({u}_{1} - {u}_{2}\right)m}{3}$

16594.sol:
By Stefan's law
If the absolute temperature of a black body is $T$, then the energy $E$ emitted per second per unit surface area of the body

$\begin{aligned}& E \propto T⁴ \\
& E=\sigma \cdotA T⁴
\end{aligned}

Given,

\begin{aligned}\sigma& =5.67 \times10^{-8} \mathrm{ W}/ \mathrm{m}^2 \mathrm{ K}^4 \\
T & =727+273=1000 \mathrm{ K}\\
A & =200 \times10^{-6} \mathrm{ m}\\
E & =5.67 \times10^{-8} \times \left(200 \times10^{-6}\right)\times(1000)^4 \\
& =5.67 \times2 \times10^{-12} \times10^{12} \\
& =11.34 \mathrm{ J}/  \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$

19541.subject: Chemistry
19541.text: Which of the following is NOT TRUE about nucleophilic addition reactions of aldehydes?
options: The hydrogensulphite addition product is useful for separation and purification of aldehydes
Aldehydes and ketones react very slowly with pure HCN to yield cyanohydrins
2,4 DNP derivatives are useful to identify aldehydes and ketones
19541.sol:
Hemiacetals contain one alkoxy group ($-OR$) and one hydroxyl group ($-OH$) attached to the same carbon atom. They are gem-alkoxyalcohols. Acetals contain two alkoxy groups attached to the same carbon atom and are known as gem-dialkoxy compounds. Thus, the statement that hemiacetals are gem-dialkoxy compounds is incorrect.

The sodium bisulphite addition product is crystalline and water-soluble, and can be converted back to the original carbonyl compound by treating it with dilute mineral acid or alkali. Therefore, it is useful for the separation and purification of aldehydes.

Pure $HCN$ reacts very slowly with aldehydes and ketones because it is a weak acid and generates cyanide ions very slowly. The reaction is typically catalyzed by a base.

2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine reacts with aldehydes and ketones to form 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazones, which are usually yellow, orange, or red solids, making them useful for characterization.

Answer: Hemiacetals are gem-dialkoxy compounds

The product formed is gluconic acid.

20794.subject: Chemistry
20794.text: Minimum mumber of nodes are present in
20794.sol:
In atomic orbitals, the number of radial nodes is given by the formula $n - l - 1$ and the number of angular nodes is given by $l$. The total number of nodes is the sum of radial and angular nodes, which is $(n - l - 1) + l = n - 1$.

For the $2s$ orbital, the principal quantum number $n = 2$ and the azimuthal quantum number $l = 0$.

Total nodes for $2s = n - 1 = 2 - 1 = 1$.

For $3s$, $n = 3$, total nodes = $3 - 1 = 2$.

For $4s$, $n = 4$, total nodes = $4 - 1 = 3$.

For $5s$, $n = 5$, total nodes = $5 - 1 = 4$.

Comparing the values, the $2s$ orbital has the minimum number of nodes.

Answer: 2 s

21544.text: $\int \dfrac{\sin 2 x}{(1+\sin x)(2+\sin x)} d x=a \log |1+\sin x|-b \log |2+\sin x|+c$ then the value of $a$ and $b$ is ----
21544.sol:
Using $\sin 2x = 2\sin x \cos x$:
$I = \int \dfrac{2\sin x \cos x}{(1+\sin x)(2+\sin x)}dx$

Let $t = \sin x$, $dt = \cos x\ dx$:
$I = \int \dfrac{2t}{(1+t)(2+t)}dt$

Partial fractions: $\dfrac{2t}{(1+t)(2+t)} = \dfrac{A}{1+t} + \dfrac{B}{2+t}$

$t = -1$: $-2 = A(1) \Rightarrow A = -2$
$t = -2$: $-4 = B(-1) \Rightarrow B = 4$

$I = \int\left(\dfrac{-2}{1+t} + \dfrac{4}{2+t}\right)dt = -2\log|1+t| + 4\log|2+t| + c$

Substituting back $t = \sin x$:
$I = -2\log|1+\sin x| + 4\log|2+\sin x| + c$

Comparing with $a\log|1+\sin x| - b\log|2+\sin x| + c$:
$a = -2$ and $-b = 4 \Rightarrow b = -4$

21911.subject: Mathematics
21911.text: A coin is tossed until a head appears or until the coin has been tossed three times. Given that 'head' does not appear on the first toss, what is the probability that the coin is tossed thrice?
21911.sol:
Let $H$ denote head and $T$ denote tail. The sample space for the experiment is $S = \{H, TH, TTH, TTT\}$.

The condition given is that head does not appear on the first toss. This means the first toss is $T$. The subset of the sample space where the first toss is $T$ is $A = \{TH, TTH, TTT\}$.

The event that the coin is tossed thrice is $B = \{TTH, TTT\}$.

We are looking for the conditional probability $P(B|A) = \dfrac{P(B \cap A)}{P(A)}$.

Since $B \subset A$, $B \cap A = B$.

The probabilities of the outcomes are:
$P(TH) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{4}$
$P(TTH) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{8}$
$P(TTT) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

$P(A) = P(TH) + P(TTH) + P(TTT) = \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{2+1+1}{8} = \dfrac{4}{8} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

$P(B) = P(TTH) + P(TTT) = \dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{1}{8} = \dfrac{2}{8} = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

$P(B|A) = \dfrac{1/4}{1/2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}$

23535.subject: Physics
23535.text: A cylinder of radius $r$ and of thermal conductivity $K_1$ is surrounded by a cylindrical shell of inner radius $r$ and outer radius $2 r$ made of a material of thermal conductivity $K_2$. The effective thermal conductivity of the system is
23535.sol:
Consider a length $L$ of the composite cylinder. The system consists of two cylindrical layers in parallel for radial heat flow. The thermal resistance $R$ of a cylindrical shell of inner radius $r_1$, outer radius $r_2$, length $L$, and thermal conductivity $K$ is given by $R = \dfrac{\ln(r_2/r_1)}{2 \pi K L}$.

For the inner cylinder of radius $r$, we consider it as a solid cylinder. However, in the context of effective thermal conductivity for radial heat flow, we treat the cross-sectional area. The total cross-sectional area $A$ of the composite cylinder is $\pi (2r)^2 = 4 \pi r^2$.

The thermal resistance of the inner cylinder of radius $r$ is $R_1 = \dfrac{\ln(r/0)}{2 \pi K_1 L}$, which is not well-defined for a solid cylinder. Instead, we use the area-weighted average conductivity for parallel heat flow across the cross-section. The effective thermal conductivity $K_{eff}$ is given by $K_{eff} = \dfrac{\sum K_i A_i}{\sum A_i}$.

The area of the inner cylinder is $A_1 = \pi r^2$. The area of the outer shell is $A_2 = \pi (2r)^2 - \pi r^2 = 3 \pi r^2$.

The total area is $A = A_1 + A_2 = 4 \pi r^2$.

Therefore, $K_{eff} = \dfrac{K_1 A_1 + K_2 A_2}{A_1 + A_2} = \dfrac{K_1 (\pi r^2) + K_2 (3 \pi r^2)}{4 \pi r^2} = \dfrac{K_1 + 3 K_2}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}(K_1 + 3 K_2)$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{4} \left(K_1+3 K_2\right)$

26518.text: A monochromatic light wave is incident normally on a glass slab of thickness $d$, as shown in the figure. The refractive index of the slab increases linearly from ${n}_{1}$ to ${n}_{2}$ over the height $h$. Which of the following statement(s) is(are) true about the light wave emerging out of the slab?

26518.sol:
Dashed line $MN$ and $PQ$ are incident wave front.

Just before entering the slab $PQ$ is maxima.

${P}_{1}$ and ${Q}_{1}$ are the points on other face of slab.

So, ${P}_{1}$ will be at a lead of ${n}_{2}d$ w.r.t. $P$

and $Q '$ will be at lead of ${n}_{1}d$ w.r.t. $Q$

As the medium on the right side is homogeneous, so to have same path lead as ${P}_{1}, Q '$ must travel to ${Q}_{1}$, such that ${n}_{2}d = {n}_{1}d + hsin\theta$.

$sin\theta = \dfrac{\left({n}_{2} - {n}_{1}\right)d}{h} ⇒ \theta = \sin^{- 1}\left[\dfrac{\left({n}_{2} - {n}_{1}\right)d}{h}\right]$

26588.text: An annular disk of mass $M$, inner radius $a$ and outer radius $b$ is placed on a horizontal surface with coefficient of friction $\mu$, as shown in the figure. At some time, an impulse ${J}_{0}\overset{∧}{x}$ is applied at a height $h$ above the center of the disk. If $h = {h}_{m}$ then the disk rolls without slipping along the $x$-axis. Which of the following statement(s) is(are) correct?
options: For $h = {h}_{m}$, the initial angular velocity does not depend on the inner radius $a$
For $\mu = 0$ and $h = 0$, the wheel always slides without rolling
26588.sol:
As we know, $\overset{\to}{J} = ∆ \overset{\to}{P}$

$⇒ {J}_{0} = MV . . . \left(i\right)$

About center of the disk, we can also write

${J}_{0} \times h = {I}_{CM}\omega ⇒ {J}_{0} \times h = \left[\dfrac{M}{2}\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2}\right)\right]\omega . . . \left(ii\right)$

If $h = {h}_{m} ⇒ \omega = \dfrac{V}{b}\left(\text{pure rolling}\right)$

From equation(ii), we can write

$⇒ {J}_{0} \times {h}_{m} = \left(\dfrac{M}{2}\right)\left({a}^{2} + {b}^{2}\right)\dfrac{V}{b} . . . \left(iii\right)$

By dividing equation $( i )$ with the equation $( iii )$, we get

$⇒ {h}_{m} = \dfrac{{a}^{2} + {b}^{2}}{2b}$

Now, considering all cases:

If $a \to 0 ⇒ {h}_{m} = \dfrac{b}{2}$

If $a \to b ⇒ {h}_{m} = b$

If $h = {h}_{m} ⇒ \omega$ is independent of $a$(As we get $\omega = \dfrac{V}{b}$)

If $\mu = 0\text{and}h = 0 ⇒$Wheel will slide without rolling.

27207.subject: Chemistry
27207.text: ' A ' is a neutral organic compound ($\mathrm{M}. \mathrm{F}: \mathrm{C}_{8} \mathrm{H}_{9} \mathrm{ON}$). On treatment with aqueous $\mathrm{Br}_{2} / \mathrm{HO}^{(-)}$, ' A ' forms a compound ' B ' which is soluble in dilute acid. ' B ' on treatment with aqueous $\mathrm{NaNO}_{2} / \mathrm{HCl}\left(0-5^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right)$ produces a compound ' C ' which on treatment with $\mathrm{CuCN} / \mathrm{NaCN}$ produces ' D '. Hydrolysis of ' D ' produces ' E ' which is also obtainable from the hydrolysis of ' A '. ' E ' on treatment with acidified $\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}$ produces ' $F$ '. ' $F$ ' contains two different types of hydrogen atoms. The structure of ' A ' is
27207.sol:
Compound A undergoes bromination with aqueous Br₂/HO⁻ to form B, which is soluble in dilute acid, indicating an amino group is present.
B undergoes diazotization with NaNO₂/HCl at 0-5°C to form diazonium compound C.
The diazonium compound is then treated with CaCN/NaOH to form nitrile compound D.
Hydrolysis of D produces carboxylic acid E.
When A is treated with acidified KMnO₄, it produces F containing two different types of hydrogen atoms.

This reaction sequence is characteristic of anthranilic acid (2-aminobenzoic acid), where the amino group directs bromination to the para position, and subsequent reactions proceed through the diazonium intermediate.

The structure shown in option (3), which is 2-aminobenzoic acid, fits all these transformations.

(1) N and As: |3.04 - 2.19| = 0.85 and |2.19 - 2.18| = 0.01. Since 0.85 > 0.01, the condition is satisfied.
(2) As and Sb: |2.18 - 2.19| = 0.01 and |2.19 - 2.05| = 0.14. Since 0.01 < 0.14, it fails.
(3) Bi and N: |2.02 - 2.19| = 0.17 and |2.19 - 3.04| = 0.85. Since 0.17 < 0.85, it fails.
(4) As and Bi: |2.18 - 2.19| = 0.01 and |2.19 - 2.02| = 0.17. Since 0.01 < 0.17, it fails.

33850.text: Let $A = \left\{z \in C: \left|\dfrac{z + 1}{z - 1}\right| < 1\right\}$ and $B = \left\{z \in C: arg\left(\dfrac{z - 1}{z + 1}\right) = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right\}$. Then $A ∩ B$ is

34384.sol:
From the given equation

$2\mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ xdx = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \tan^{- 1} ⁡ \left(1 - x + {x}^{2}\right)\right)dx$

$⇒ 2\mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ xdx = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{\pi}{2}dx - \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ \left(1 - x + {x}^{2}\right)dx$
$⇒ \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ \left(1 - x + {x}^{2}\right)dx = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 2\mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ xdx \ldots \left(i\right)$
Let ${I}_{1} = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ xdx$

$= {\left[\left(\tan^{- 1} ⁡ x\right)x\right]}_{0}^{1} - \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{1}{1 + {x}^{2}}xdx$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{x}{1 + {x}^{2}}dx$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}\mathop{∫}_{0}^{1}\dfrac{2x}{1 + {x}^{2}}dx$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}{\left[ln\left(1 + {x}^{2}\right)\right]}_{0}^{1}$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}ln ⁡ 2$

By equation $\left(i\right)$,

${∫}_{0}^{1}\tan^{- 1} ⁡ \left(1 - x + {x}^{2}\right)dx = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 2\left[\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}ln2\right] = ln ⁡ 2$

$x + y + az = b$

$x - y + z = 3$

Now $∵ y\left(0\right) = 0$

$⇒ C = 0$

36327.text: A box contains $5$ blue, $6$ yellow and $4$ red balls. The number of ways, of drawing $8$ balls containing at least two balls of each colour, is :
36327.sol:
Let $B$, $Y$, and $R$ be the number of blue, yellow, and red balls drawn respectively.

We are given $B + Y + R = 8$ with $B \ge 2$, $Y \ge 2$, and $R \ge 2$.

The possible combinations for $(B, Y, R)$ are:
Case 1: $(2, 2, 4)$
Case 2: $(2, 3, 3)$
Case 3: $(2, 4, 2)$
Case 4: $(3, 2, 3)$
Case 5: $(3, 3, 2)$
Case 6: $(4, 2, 2)$

The number of ways for each case is calculated as follows:
Case 1: $^{5}C_{2} \times ^{6}C_{2} \times ^{4}C_{4} = 10 \times 15 \times 1 = 150$
Case 2: $^{5}C_{2} \times ^{6}C_{3} \times ^{4}C_{3} = 10 \times 20 \times 4 = 800$
Case 3: $^{5}C_{2} \times ^{6}C_{4} \times ^{4}C_{2} = 10 \times 15 \times 6 = 900$
Case 4: $^{5}C_{3} \times ^{6}C_{2} \times ^{4}C_{3} = 10 \times 15 \times 4 = 600$
Case 5: $^{5}C_{3} \times ^{6}C_{3} \times ^{4}C_{2} = 10 \times 20 \times 6 = 1200$
Case 6: $^{5}C_{4} \times ^{6}C_{2} \times ^{4}C_{2} = 5 \times 15 \times 6 = 450$

Total number of ways $= 150 + 800 + 900 + 600 + 1200 + 450 = 4100$

Answer: $4100$

37170.sol:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = 2{x}^{2} - x - 1$ and $\left|f\left(n\right)\right| \le 800$

So, $2{n}^{2} - n - 801 \le 0$

$⇒ {n}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}n - \dfrac{801}{2} \le 0$

$⇒ {\left(n - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2} - \dfrac{801}{2} - \dfrac{1}{16} \le 0$

$⇒ {\left(n - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{2} - \dfrac{6409}{16} \le 0$

$⇒ \left(n - \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{\sqrt{6409}}{4}\right)\left(n - \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{\sqrt{6409}}{16}\right) \le 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{1 - \sqrt{6409}}{4} \le n \le \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{6409}}{4}$

Since given $n$ is integer,

So, $n = \left\{- 19, - 18 - 17, \ldots \ldots . . 0, 1, 2, \ldots \ldots , 20\right\}$

Now $\mathop{∑}_{n \in S}f\left(x\right) = ∑ \left(2{x}^{2} - x - 1\right)$

$= \left(2 ∑ {x}^{2} - ∑ x - ∑ 1\right)$

$= 2\left[{19}^{2} + {18}^{2} + \ldots . + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {2}^{2} + \ldots . + {19}^{2} + {20}^{2}\right] - 20 - 40$ $\left(\text{as} ∑ x = 20 \text{ and } ∑ 1 = 40\right)$

$= 4\left[{1}^{2} + {2}^{2} + \ldots . . + {19}^{2}\right] + 2\left[{20}^{2}\right] - 20 - 40$

$= \dfrac{4 \times 19 \times 20 \times \left(2 \times 19 + 1\right)}{6} + 2 \times 400 - 60$

$= \dfrac{4 \times 19 \times 20 \times 39}{6} + 800 - 60 - 9880 + 800 - 60$

$= 10620$

38023.text: Let the plane $P$ pass through the intersection of the planes $2x + 3y - z = 2 and x + 2y + 3z = 6$, and be perpendicular to the plane $2x + y - z + 1 = 0$. If $d$ is the distance of $P$ from the point $\left(- 7, 1, 1\right)$, then ${d}^{2}$ is equal to :
38023.sol:
A plane $P$ pass through the intersection of planes ${P}_{1} and {P}_{2}$ can be written as,

$P ≡ {P}_{1} + \lambda{P}_{2} = 0$

$\left(2 + \lambda\right)x + \left(3 + 2\lambda\right)y + \left(3\lambda - 1\right)z - \left(2 + 6\lambda\right) = 0$

Given, $P ⊥ {P}_{3} ( 2x + y - z + 1 = 0 )$

$∴ \overset{\to}{n} . \overset{\to}{n}3 = 0$

$⇒ 2\left(\lambda + 2\right) + \left(2\lambda + 3\right) - \left(3\lambda - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ 4 + 2\lambda + 2\lambda + 3 - 3\lambda + 1 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = - 8$

$∴ P ≡ - 6x - 13y - 25z + 46 = 0$

$6x + 13y + 25z - 46 = 0$

Since, the distance $d$ from $( {x}_{0}, {y}_{0}, {z}_{0} )$ to the plane $Ax + By + Cz + D = 0$ is,

$d = \dfrac{\left|A{x}_{0} + B{y}_{0} + C{z}_{0} + D\right|}{\sqrt{{A}^{2} + {B}^{2} + {C}^{2}}}$

Now the distance of plane $P$ from point $\left(- 7, 1, 1\right)$,

$d = \dfrac{\left|- 42 + 13 + 25 - 46\right|}{\sqrt{36 + 169 + 625}} = \dfrac{50}{\sqrt{830}}$

$∴ {d}^{2} = \dfrac{50 \times 50}{830} = \dfrac{250}{83}$

39100.subject: Physics
39100.text: A parallel plate capacitor with plate separation 5 mm is charged by a battery. On introducing a mica sheet of 2 mm and maintaining the connections of the plates with the terminals of the battery, it is found that it draws $25 \%$ more charge from the battery. The dielectric constant of mica is $\_\_\_\_$.
39100.sol:
Initial capacitor has plate separation 5 mm with capacitance $C_1 = \epsilon_0 A / 5$.
After inserting 2 mm mica sheet, the gap remaining is 3 mm of air. The effective separation becomes: $d_{eff} = 3 + 2/k$ where $k$ is the dielectric constant of mica.
New capacitance: $C_2 = \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{3 + 2/k}$
Since battery remains connected, voltage is constant. The charge is: $Q = CV$
Ratio of charges: $\frac{Q_2}{Q_1} = \frac{C_2}{C_1} = \frac{\epsilon_0 A/(3 + 2/k)}{\epsilon_0 A/5} = \frac{5}{3 + 2/k}$
Given that charge increases by 25%: $Q_2 = 1.25 Q_1$
$\frac{5}{3 + 2/k} = 1.25$
$5 = 1.25(3 + 2/k)$
$5 = 3.75 + 2.5/k$
$1.25 = 2.5/k$
$k = 2$

39508.subject: Physics
39508.text: Refer to the circuit diagram given below. The heat generated across the $6\,\Omega$ resistance in $100$ second is $\dfrac{\alpha}{100}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is _______. (Nearest integer)
39508.sol:
Taking the right-hand wire as the reference node at $0\text{ V}$, let the left junction (where the $3\,\Omega$, $4\,\Omega$ and $6\,\Omega$ resistors meet) be Node A at potential $V_A$.

Bottom branch: The positive terminal of the $2\text{ V}$ battery is at the reference, so its negative terminal (and hence the left end of the $3\,\Omega$ resistor) is at $-2\text{ V}$.
Top branch: The positive terminal of the $3\text{ V}$ battery is at the reference, so its negative terminal (and hence the node between the $6\,\Omega$ resistor and the $3\text{ V}$ battery) is at $-3\text{ V}$.

Applying KCL at Node A (sum of currents leaving the node is zero):
$\dfrac{V_A - 0}{4} + \dfrac{V_A - (-2)}{3} + \dfrac{V_A - (-3)}{6} = 0$

$\dfrac{V_A}{4} + \dfrac{V_A + 2}{3} + \dfrac{V_A + 3}{6} = 0$

Multiplying throughout by $12$:
$3V_A + 4(V_A + 2) + 2(V_A + 3) = 0$

$3V_A + 4V_A + 8 + 2V_A + 6 = 0$

$9V_A + 14 = 0 \Rightarrow V_A = -\dfrac{14}{9}\text{ V}$

Current through the $6\,\Omega$ resistor (from Node A towards the $-3\text{ V}$ point):
$I_6 = \dfrac{V_A - (-3)}{6} = \dfrac{-\dfrac{14}{9} + 3}{6} = \dfrac{\dfrac{13}{9}}{6} = \dfrac{13}{54}\text{ A}$

Heat generated in the $6\,\Omega$ resistor in $t = 100\text{ s}$:
$H = I_6^2 \cdot R \cdot t = \left(\dfrac{13}{54}\right)^2 \cdot 6 \cdot 100$

$H = \dfrac{169}{2916} \cdot 600 = \dfrac{169 \cdot 100}{486} = \dfrac{16900}{486}\text{ J}$

Given $H = \dfrac{\alpha}{100}\text{ J}$:
$\dfrac{\alpha}{100} = \dfrac{16900}{486}$

$\alpha = \dfrac{16900 \cdot 100}{486} = \dfrac{1690000}{486} \approx 3477.37$

Rounding to the nearest integer:
$\alpha = 3477$

Hence, the answer is $3477$.

39923.text: When a light of a given wavelength falls on a metallic surface the stopping potential for photoelectrons is 3.2 V. If a second light having wavelength twice of first light is used, the stopping potential drops to 0.7 V. The wavelength of first light is $\_\_\_\_$ m. $\left(\mathrm{h}=6.63 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{~J}. \mathrm{s}, \mathrm{e}=1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}, \mathrm{c}=3 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\right)$
39923.sol:
Using Einstein's photoelectric equation with stopping potentials:
For first light, $h u_1 = \phi + eV_{s1}$.
For second light with $\lambda_2 = 2\lambda_1$ (so $ u_2 = u_1/2$): $h u_1/2 = \phi + eV_{s2}$.
From given values: $h u_1 - 3.2e = h u_1/2 - 0.7e$ gives $h u_1/2 = 2.5e$.
Thus $\lambda_1 = rac{hc}{5e} = rac{6.63 imes 10^{-34} imes 3 imes 10^8}{5 imes 1.6 imes 10^{-19}} \approx 2.5 imes 10^{-7}$ m.

39956.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion $\mathbf{A}$ and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: Number of photons increases with increase in frequency of light.
Reason R: Maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons increases with the frequency of incident radiation.

options: Both $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ are correct and $\mathbf{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\mathbf{A}$.
Both $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ are correct and $\mathbf{R}$ is NOT the correct explanation of $\mathbf{A}$.
$\mathbf{A}$ is not correct but $\mathbf{R}$ is correct.
$\mathbf{A}$ is correct but $\mathbf{R}$ is not correct.
39956.sol:
Intensity of light $\mathrm{I}=\frac{\mathrm{nh} \nu}{\mathrm{A}}$ Here $\mathrm{n}$ is no. of photons per unit time. $\mathrm{n}=\frac{\mathrm{IA}}{\mathrm{h} \nu}$ so on increasing frequency $v, \mathrm{n}$ decreases taking intensity constant. $\mathrm{k}_{\max }=\mathrm{h} v-\phi$
So on increasing $v$, kinetic energy increases.

43239.text: A solid sphere of mass $2kg$ is making pure rolling on a horizontal surface with kinetic energy $2240J$. The velocity of centre of mass of the sphere will be ______ $m{s}^{- 1}$.
43239.sol:
Let velocity of centre of mass of sphere be $v$.

Total kinetic energy of solid sphere is $KE = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2}$, where, $I$ is moment of inertia of the solid sphere about the axis passing through it's centre of mass and $\omega = \dfrac{v}{R}\left(\text{pure rolling condition}\right)$.

Therefore,

$2240 = \dfrac{1}{2}2 ( v{)}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{2}{5} ( 2 ) {R}^{2}\right]{\left(\dfrac{v}{R}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ 2240 = {v}^{2} + \dfrac{2}{5}{v}^{2}$

$⇒ v = 40m{s}^{- 1}$.

46242.text: A certain charge $Q$ is divided into two parts $q$ and $Q-q$. How the charge $Q$ and $q$ must be related so that when $q$ and $(Q-q)$ is placed at a certain distance apart experience maximum electrostatic repulsion?
46242.sol:
The electrostatic force of repulsion between the charge $q$ and $(Q-q)$ at separation $r$ is given by
$F=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{q(Q-q)}{r^2}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{q Q-q^2}{r^2}$
If $F$ is maximum, then $\partial F / \partial q=0$ i.e. $\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{(Q-2 q)}{r^2}=0$
As $\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 r^2}$ is constant, therefore
$Q-2 q=0$ or $Q=2 q$

$\begin{array}{rlrl}v & =4 v_p \\ \therefore & A \omega & =4 \frac{\omega}{k} \\ \therefore & y_0 \omega & =\frac{4 \omega}{k} \\ \Rightarrow & & y_0=\frac{4}{k} & =\frac{4}{2 \pi} \times \lambda\end{array}$
Therefore, wavelength $\lambda=\frac{\pi y_0}{2}$

As man alight, its angular momentum about a point on platform is conserved.

By angular momentum conservation,

${L}_{initial} = {L}_{final} ⇒ mvr = I\omega$

$⇒ mvr = \dfrac{ml^{2}}{3} \cdot \omega ⇒ \dfrac{3vr}{l2} = \omega$

or $\omega = \dfrac{3 \times 2 \times \left(\dfrac{1. 5}{2}\right)}{\left(1. 5\right)^{2}} = 2rad / s$

So, instantaneous angular speed of man $= 2rad / s$.

54848.subject: Chemistry
54848.text: Which from the following is a correct decreasing order of boiling points for following organic compounds ?
54848.sol:
Boiling point depends on the strength of intermolecular forces.

Carboxylic acids form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds and exist as dimers, leading to the highest boiling points among compounds of comparable molecular mass.

Alcohols also form intermolecular hydrogen bonds, but they are weaker than those in carboxylic acids.

Ketones and aldehydes lack intermolecular hydrogen bonding but possess dipole-dipole interactions.

Ketones have slightly higher boiling points than isomeric aldehydes due to the presence of two electron-donating alkyl groups, which makes the carbonyl group more polar, resulting in stronger dipole-dipole interactions.

Thus, the correct decreasing order of boiling points is Carboxylic acid > Alcohol > Ketone > Aldehyde.

Answer: Carboxylic acid > Alcohol > Ketone > Aldehyde

57600.subject: Chemistry
57600.text: Identify the product formed when 2-Bromobutane is heated with aqueous solution of sodium hydroxide.
57600.sol:
2-Bromobutane ($\mathrm{CH_3CH(Br)CH_2CH_3}$) is a secondary alkyl halide reacting with sodium hydroxide, a strong nucleophile and base, in aqueous solution under heating. The polar protic solvent facilitates solvation and favors nucleophilic substitution.

Hydroxide ion attacks the electrophilic carbon, displacing bromide via $\mathrm{S_N2}$: $\mathrm{CH_3CH(Br)CH_2CH_3 + OH- \rightarrow CH_3CH(OH)CH_2CH_3 + Br^-}$, yielding butan-2-ol.

Concurrently, elimination may occur via $\mathrm{E2}$, abstracting a $\beta$-hydrogen to form either but-1-ene or but-2-ene: $\mathrm{CH_3CH(Br)CH_2CH_3 + OH- \rightarrow CH_3CH=CHCH_3 + H_2 O + Br^-}$ or $\mathrm{CH_3CH(Br)CH_2CH_3 + OH- \rightarrow CH_2=CHCH_2CH_3 + H_2 O + Br^-}$. Zaitsev's rule predicts but-2-ene as the major elimination product.

In aqueous solvent, $\mathrm{S_N2}$ dominates over $\mathrm{E2}$ due to solvation effects that stabilize the substitution transition state. Butan-2-ol is thus the major product.

Final Answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

58575.text: Which among the following statements about terpenes is NOT true?
options: Terpenes include vitamin A, E and $\mathrm{K}$
58575.sol:
Terpenes are hydrocarbons that are classified by the number of isoprene units (C5H8), with the most common being mono-, sesqui-, and di-terpenes (C10, C15, and C20, respectively).
Terpenes are highly aromatic compounds that determine the smell of many plants and herbs, such as rosemary and lavender, as well as some animals. Manufacturers use isolated terpenes to create the flavors and scents of many everyday products, such as perfumes, body products, and even foods.
The side chains of Vitamin A, E, K, squalene (unsaturated hydrocarbon found in shark, humans) are all constituents of terpenes.
Terpenes are important constituents of essential oils, having a chemical structure consisting of repeated isoprene $\left(\mathrm{C}_{5} \mathrm{H}_{8}\right)$ units. They are classified into monoterpenes $\left(C_{10}\right)$, sesquiterpenes $\left(C_{15}\right)$, and diterpenes $\left(C_{20}\right)$ based on whether they are made up of two, three, or four isoprene units respectively.

61016.subject: Mathematics
61016.text: The value of integral $\int_0^\infty \dfrac{1}{1 + e^x}\,dx$ is...
61016.sol:
Let $I = \int_0^\infty \dfrac{1}{1 + e^x} dx$

Multiplying the numerator and the denominator by $e^{-x}$:

$I = \int_0^\infty \dfrac{e^{-x}}{e^{-x} + 1} dx$

Let $e^{-x} + 1 = t$

Differentiating both sides, $-e^{-x} dx = dt \Rightarrow e^{-x} dx = -dt$

Limits of integration:

When $x = 0$, $t = e^0 + 1 = 2$

When $x \to \infty$, $t = e^{-\infty} + 1 = 1$

Substituting these into the integral:

$I = \int_2^1 \dfrac{-dt}{t} = \int_1^2 \dfrac{dt}{t}$

$I = [\log t]_1^2 = \log 2 - \log 1 = \log 2$

Answer: $\log 2$

61320.text: The rate of increase of the population of a city is proportional to the population present at that instant. In the period of 40 years the population increased from 30,000 to 40,000. At any time $t$ the population is $(a)(b)^{\frac{t}{40}}$. Then the value of $a$ and $b$ are respectively
61320.sol:
The population growth follows the differential equation $\frac{dP}{dt} = kP$, leading to the solution $P(t) = P_0 e^{kt}$ with $P_0 = 30,000$.

Using the condition $P(40) = 40,000$, we get $40,000 = 30,000 e^{40k}$, so $e^{40k} = \frac{4}{3}$.

Rewriting $P(t) = 30,000 e^{kt}$ as $P(t) = 30,000 (e^{40k})^{\frac{t}{40}}$, then $P(t) = 30,000 \left(\frac{4}{3}\right)^{\frac{t}{40}}$.

This matches the form $(a)(b)^{\frac{t}{40}}$ with $a = 30,000$ and $b = \frac{4}{3}$, corresponding to option B.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

61329.text: The integrating factor of $\mathrm{y}+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} x}(x \mathrm{y})=x(\sin x+\log x)$ is
61329.sol:
Rewriting the given differential equation $y + \frac{d}{dx}(xy) = x(\sin x + \log x)$ in standard form, we apply the product rule to $\frac{d}{dx}(xy)$ yielding $y + x\frac{dy}{dx}$.

Substituting gives $y + y + x\frac{dy}{dx} = x(\sin x + \log x)$ or $2y + x\frac{dy}{dx} = x(\sin x + \log x)$.

Dividing by $x$ produces $\frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{2}{x}y = \sin x + \log x$, revealing $P(x) = \frac{2}{x}$.

The integrating factor is $e^{\int P(x) dx} = e^{\int \frac{2}{x} dx} = e^{2\log|x|} = x^2$.

Final Answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

Comparing with the standard equation $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$, we have $a^2 = 100$ and $b^2 = 144$.

The given line is $y = 2x + \lambda$. Comparing with $y = mx + c$, we have $m = 2$ and $c = \lambda$.

The condition for a line to be tangent to a hyperbola is $c^2 = a^2m^2 - b^2$.

Substituting the values, we get:

$\lambda^2 = 100(2)^2 - 144$

$\lambda^2 = 400 - 144$

$\lambda^2 = 256$

$\lambda = \pm 16$

Answer: $\pm 16$

63330.subject: Mathematics
63330.text: The joint equation of the pair of lines through the origin and making an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ with the line $3x + y - 6 = 0$ is
63330.sol:
Slope of the given line $3x + y - 6 = 0$ is $m_1 = -3$.

Let $m$ be the slope of a line passing through the origin and making an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ with the given line.

Using the angle formula, $\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \left| \dfrac{m - m_1}{1 + m m_1} \right|$

$1 = \left| \dfrac{m - (-3)}{1 + m(-3)} \right| = \left| \dfrac{m + 3}{1 - 3m} \right|$

Squaring both sides, we get:

$(1 - 3m)^2 = (m + 3)^2$

$1 - 6m + 9m^2 = m^2 + 6m + 9$

$8m^2 - 12m - 8 = 0$

Dividing by $4$, we get $2m^2 - 3m - 2 = 0$.

Since the lines pass through the origin, their equations are of the form $y = mx$, which implies $m = \dfrac{y}{x}$.

Substituting $m = \dfrac{y}{x}$ in the quadratic equation:

$2\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right)^2 - 3\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) - 2 = 0$

$2y^2 - 3xy - 2x^2 = 0$

Multiplying by $-1$, we obtain the joint equation:

$2x^2 + 3xy - 2y^2 = 0$.

Answer: $2x^2 + 3xy - 2y^2 = 0$

63998.text: If two sides of a triangle are $\sqrt{3}-$2$ and \sqrt{3}+2$ units and their included angle is $60^{{}^{\circ}}$, then the third side of the triangle is
63998.sol:
Given two sides of a triangle as $a = \sqrt{3} - 2$ and $b = \sqrt{3} + 2$, with included angle $C = 60^{{}^{\circ}}$, the third side $c$ is found using the Law of Cosines: $c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab \cos C$.

Compute $a^2 = (\sqrt{3} - 2)^2 = 7 - 4\sqrt{3}$, $b^2 = (\sqrt{3} + 2)^2 = 7 + 4\sqrt{3}$, and $ab = (\sqrt{3} - 2)(\sqrt{3} + 2) = -1$.

Substitute into the formula with $\cos 60^{{}^{\circ}} = \frac{1}{2}$:

$c^2 = (7 - 4\sqrt{3}) + (7 + 4\sqrt{3}) - 2(-1)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 14 + 1 = 15$.

Thus, $c = \sqrt{15}$.

Comparing with the options, the length is $\sqrt{15} units.

64411.subject: Mathematics
64411.text: The equation of plane passing through $(1,0,0)$ and $(0,1,0)$ and making an angle $45^{{}^{\circ}}$ with the plane $x+y-3=0$ is
64411.sol:
The required plane passes through $(1, 0, 0) and (0, 1, 0)$, and makes a $45^{}^{\circ}$ angle with the plane $x + y - 3 = 0$. Let the general equation be $Ax + By + Cz + D = 0$.

Substituting $(1, 0, 0)$ gives $A + D = 0 \Rightarrow A = -D$.
Substituting $(0, 1, 0)$ gives $B + D = 0 \Rightarrow B = -D$.

Using these, the equation becomes $-Dx - Dy + Cz + D = 0$.
For $D \neq 0$, divide by $D$: $-x - y + \frac{C}{D}z + 1 = 0$.
Let $k = \frac{C}{D}$, so the plane becomes $x + y - kz - 1 = 0$.

The normal vector is $\vec{n}_1 = (1, 1, -k)$.
The given plane $x + y - 3 = 0$ has normal vector $\vec{n}_2 = (1, 1, 0)$.

The angle $\theta$ between planes satisfies $\cos\theta = \frac{|\vec{n}_1 \cdot \vec{n}_2|}{\|\vec{n}_1\| \|\vec{n}_2\|}$.
Given $\theta = 45^{}^{\circ}$, so $\cos45^{}^{\circ} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

Compute:
$\vec{n}_1 \cdot \vec{n}_2 = 1 \cdot 1 + 1 \cdot 1 + (-k) \cdot 0 = 2$
$\|\vec{n}_1\| = \sqrt{1^2 + 1^2 + (-k)^2} = \sqrt{2 + k^2}$
$\|\vec{n}_2\| = \sqrt{1^2 + 1^2 + 0^2} = \sqrt{2}$

Substitute into the formula:
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{2 + k^2} \cdot \sqrt{2}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{2(2 + k^2)}}$

Square both sides:
$\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{2(2 + k^2)}}\right)^2 \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} = \frac{4}{2(2 + k^2)} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{2 + k^2}$

Cross-multiplying: $2 + k^2 = 4 \Rightarrow k^2 = 2 \Rightarrow k = \pm\sqrt{2}$

Substitute back into the plane equation:
$x + y - (\sqrt{2})z - 1 = 0 or x + y + \sqrt{2}z - 1 = 0$
Thus, the required plane is $x + y \pm \sqrt{2}z - 1 = 0$, corresponding to option A.

66757.subject: Physics
66757.text: Two coils A and B have 180 and 360 turns respectively. The current of 1A flows through both the coils. Due to current of 1A in coil A, flux per turn of $0.8 \times 10^{-3}$ Wb is linked with coil A. Due to current of 1A in coil B, flux per turn of $1 \times 10^{-3}$ Wb is linked with coil B. The self inductance of coil A is $L_A$ and the self inductance of coil B is $L_B$. The ratio $L_A$ to $L_B$ is
66757.sol:
The self-inductance of a coil is given by $L = \dfrac{N \phi}{I}$, where $N$ is the number of turns, $\phi$ is the flux per turn, and $I$ is the current.

For coil A:
$L_A = \dfrac{N_A \phi_A}{I_A} = \dfrac{180 \times 0.8 \times 10^{-3}}{1} = 144 \times 10^{-3}$ H

For coil B:
$L_B = \dfrac{N_B \phi_B}{I_B} = \dfrac{360 \times 1 \times 10^{-3}}{1} = 360 \times 10^{-3}$ H

The ratio of their self-inductances is:
$\dfrac{L_A}{L_B} = \dfrac{144 \times 10^{-3}}{360 \times 10^{-3}} = \dfrac{144}{360} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{5}$

67031.text: Charges of $2 \mu \mathrm{C}$ and $-3 \mu \mathrm{C}$ are placed at two points $A$ and $B$ separated by distance of 1 m. The distance of the point from $A$ where net potential is zero is
67031.sol:
Let charges be $q_A = 2\,\mu\mathrm{C}$ and $q_B = -3\,\mu\mathrm{C}$ separated by distance $d = 1\,\mathrm{m}$. To find a point with zero net electric potential, consider possible regions and use $V = \frac{kq}{r}$ formulation.

Case 1: Between the charges
Let point P be at distance $x$ from A, so distance from B is $1 - x$. The net potential $V_P = \frac{kq_A}{x} + \frac{kq_B}{1 - x} = 0$ yields $\frac{2}{x} = \frac{3}{1 - x}$, resulting in $2(1 - x) = 3x$ and $x = 0.4\,\mathrm{m}$. This point lies between A and B.

Case 2: Outside the charges
Let P be left of A with distance $x$ to A and $1 + x$ to B. Setting $V_P = 0$ gives $\frac{2}{x} = \frac{3}{1 + x}$, solved by $2(1 + x) = 3x$ and $x = 2\,\mathrm{m}$, a valid point to the left of A.

Comparing with options, $x = 0.4\,\mathrm{m}$ corresponds to option C.

Final answer: $\boxed{0.4\ \mathrm{m}}$

70522.text: When two tuning forks are sounded together, 6 beats per second are heard. One of the fork is in unison with 0.70 m length of sonometer wire and another fork is in unison with 0.69 m length of the same sonometer wire. The frequencies of the two tuning forks are
70522.sol:
When two tuning forks produce 6 beats per second, the difference in their frequencies is 6 Hz: $|f_1 - f_2| = 6$.

The frequency of a vibrating sonometer wire is inversely proportional to its length, $f \propto 1/L$, so $fL$ remains constant for constant tension and linear density. Given $L_1 = 0.70 \text{ m}$ and $L_2 = 0.69 \text{ m}$, the frequencies satisfy $f_1 L_1 = f_2 L_2$.

Since $L_1 > L_2$, it follows that $f_1 < f_2$, so the beat frequency equation becomes $f_2 - f_1 = 6$.

Substitute $f_1 = f_2 L_2 / L_1$ into the beat equation: $f_2 - (0.69 / 0.70) f_2 = 6$. Simplify to $f_2 (1 - 0.69 / 0.70) = 6$, yielding $f_2 (0.01 / 0.70) = 6$. Solve for $f_2 = 6 \times 0.70 / 0.01 = 420 \text{ Hz}$.

Then $f_1 = 420 - 6 = 414 \text{ Hz}$.

The frequencies are $414 \text{ Hz}$ and $420 \text{ Hz}$, corresponding to option B.

The answer is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

71040.subject: Biology
71040.text: Which of the following statements is FALSE about the Phosphorus Cycle?
options: Atmospheric inputs of phosphorus through rainfall are meagre.
Gaseous exchange of phosphorus between organisms and the environment are negligible.
Phosphorus does not act as a limiting factor for plant growth.
Agricultural runoff rich in phosphate content leads to eutrophication.
71040.sol:
Analyzing each statement regarding the Phosphorus Cycle:

Statement (1): Unlike the carbon cycle, atmospheric inputs of phosphorus through rainfall are indeed much smaller. This statement is true.

Statement (2): Phosphorus is a sedimentary cycle. There is no significant respiratory release or gaseous phase for phosphorus, meaning gaseous exchange between organisms and the environment is negligible. This statement is true.

Statement (3): Phosphorus is an essential macronutrient for plants. In many ecosystems, its availability in the soil is low, often making it a major limiting factor for plant growth. Thus, the statement 'Phosphorus does not act as a limiting factor for plant growth' is false.

Statement (4): Runoff from agricultural fields containing high amounts of phosphate fertilizers enriches water bodies with nutrients, accelerating the growth of algae and leading to eutrophication. This statement is true.

Therefore, the false statement is (3).

Answer: Phosphorus does not act as a limiting factor for plant growth.

71200.subject: Biology
71200.text: Identify the INCORRECT statement about zona pellucida.
options: It has fertilizin receptor proteins (ZP 3, ZP 2)
The fertilizin binds to specific protein- antifertilizin of sperm.
It brings about attraction of sperms to the egg to enhance fertilization.
It stimulates acrosome to release Trypsin and Pepin
71200.sol:
The zona pellucida contains glycoproteins such as ZP1, ZP2, and ZP3. ZP3 acts as a primary sperm receptor and binds to specific proteins on the sperm head, which triggers the acrosome reaction.

The fertilizin-antifertilizin interaction is a species-specific reaction where fertilizin (secreted by the egg) binds to antifertilizin (present on the sperm), facilitating the attraction and agglutination of sperms to enhance fertilization.

During the acrosome reaction, the acrosome releases sperm lysins, which include hyaluronidase, corona penetrating enzyme, and acrosin (a trypsin-like enzyme). It does not release trypsin and pepsin (gastric enzymes). Therefore, the statement that it stimulates the acrosome to release trypsin and pepsin is incorrect.

Answer: It stimulates acrosome to release Trypsin and Pepin

72203.subject: Physics
72203.text: A uniform electric field is given as $\vec{E} = 4 \times 10^4\,\hat{j}\ \text{N/C}$. The flux of this field through a square of side $10\ \text{cm}$ whose plane is parallel to the Y-Z plane is
72203.sol:
The electric field is given as $\vec{E} = 4 \times 10^4\,\hat{j}\ \text{N/C}$.

The area of the square is $A = (10\ \text{cm})^2 = 0.01\ \text{m}^2$.

Since the plane of the square is parallel to the Y-Z plane, its area vector is perpendicular to the Y-Z plane, which means it is directed along the X-axis.

$\vec{A} = 0.01\,\hat{i}\ \text{m}^2$

The electric flux $\Phi$ through the square is given by the dot product of the electric field and the area vector:

$\Phi = \vec{E} \cdot \vec{A}$

$\Phi = (4 \times 10^4\,\hat{j}) \cdot (0.01\,\hat{i})$

Since $\hat{j} \cdot \hat{i} = 0$, we get:

$\Phi = 0$

Answer: zero

72233.subject: Physics
72233.text:
The temperature at which the root-mean-square speed of carbon dioxide molecules becomes just sufficient for escaping Earth's atmosphere is approximately
(Mass of carbon dioxide molecule $= 7 \times 10^{-26}\ \text{kg}$, Boltzmann's constant $k_B = 14 \times 10^{-24}\ J/K$, escape velocity from Earth's surface $= 11\ \text{km/s}$)
72233.sol:
The root-mean-square speed of gas molecules is given by:

$v_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3 k_B T}{m}}$

For the molecules to escape Earth's atmosphere, their rms speed must be equal to the escape velocity $v_e$:

$\sqrt{\dfrac{3 k_B T}{m}} = v_e$

Squaring both sides and solving for $T$:

$T = \dfrac{m v_e^2}{3 k_B}$

Substituting the given values ($m = 7 \times 10^{-26}\ \text{kg}$, $v_e = 11 \times 10^3\ \text{m/s}$, $k_B = 14 \times 10^{-24}\ \text{J/K}$):

$T = \dfrac{7 \times 10^{-26} \times (11 \times 10^3)^2}{3 \times 14 \times 10^{-24}}$

$T = \dfrac{7 \times 121 \times 10^{-20}}{42 \times 10^{-24}}$

$T = \dfrac{121}{6} \times 10^4$

$T \approx 20.166 \times 10^4\ \text{K}$

$T \approx 2.016 \times 10^5\ \text{K}$

Answer: $2.016 \times 10^5\ \text{K}$

76647.subject: Mathematics
76647.text: If $x + \dfrac{1}{x} = 2\cos\theta$, then what is $x^3 + \dfrac{1}{x^3}$ equal to?
76647.sol:
Given $x + \dfrac{1}{x} = 2\cos\theta$

Using the algebraic identity $a^3 + b^3 = (a+b)^3 - 3ab(a+b)$:

$x^3 + \dfrac{1}{x^3} = \left(x + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^3 - 3 \left($x + $\dfrac{1}{x}\right)

Substituting $ x + $\dfrac{1}{x} =2\$ cos\theta:

$ x^3 + \dfrac{1}{x^3} = ( 2\cos\theta)^3 -3(2\cos\theta)$

$x^3 + \dfrac{1}{x^3} =8\$cos^3\theta -$6\$cos\theta

$x^3 + \dfrac{1}{x^3} = 2(4\cos^3\theta -3\cos\theta)$

Using the trigonometric identity $\cos 3\theta =4\$ cos^3\theta -$3\$cos\theta:

$x^3 + \dfrac{1}{x^3} =$2$\cos 3\theta$

Answer: 2$\cos 3\theta

77997.subject: Mathematics
77997.text: If $P(A) = \dfrac{1}{3}$, $P(B) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $P(A \cap B) = \dfrac{1}{4}$, then what is the value of $P(A^c \cap B^c)$?
77997.sol:
Using the formula for the probability of the union of two events:

$P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$

Substituting the given values:

$P(A \cup B) = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{4}$

$P(A \cup B) = \dfrac{4 + 6 - 3}{12} = \dfrac{7}{12}$

By De Morgan's laws, $A^c \cap B^c = (A \cup B)^c$.

Therefore, the probability is:

$P(A^c \cap B^c) = 1 - P(A \cup B)$

$P(A^c \cap B^c) = 1 - \dfrac{7}{12} = \dfrac{5}{12}$

78643.subject: Mathematics
78643.text: Two variates, x and y , are uncorrelated and have standard deviations $\sigma_x$ and $\sigma_y$ respectively. What is the correlation coefficient between $\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}$ and $\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{y}$ ?
78643.sol:
Let $u=(x+y) ; v=(x-y)\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \bar{u}=(\bar{x}+\bar{y}) ; \bar{v}=(\bar{x}-\bar{y}) \\
& \operatorname{cov}(u, v)=E\{(u-\bar{u})(v-\bar{v})\} \\
& =E\{(x-\bar{x})+(y-\bar{y})\} \cdot\{(x-\bar{x})-(y-\bar{y})\} \\
& =E\left\{(x-\bar{x})^2-(y-\bar{y})^2\right\}=\sigma_x^2-\sigma_y^2 \\
& \operatorname{var}(u)=E(u-\bar{u})^2=E\{(x-\bar{x})+(y-\bar{y})\}^2=\sigma_x^2+\sigma_y^2
\end{aligned}$
Therefore $x and y$ are uncorrelated.
$E(x-\bar{x})(y-\bar{y})=0$
Similarly, $\operatorname{var}(v)=\sigma_x^2+\sigma_y^2$
Thus, $r(u, v)=\frac{\operatorname{cov}(u, v)}{\sqrt{\operatorname{var}(u) \cdot \operatorname{var}(v)}}=\frac{\sigma_x^2-\sigma_y^2}{\sigma_x^2+\sigma_y^2}$

Let $p = |\sin\alpha - \sin(\alpha - 90°)|$.

Given $p = |\sin\alpha - \sin(\alpha - 90^{}^{\circ})|$

Using the trigonometric identity $\sin(\alpha - 90^{}^{\circ}) = -\sin(90^{}^{\circ} - \alpha) = -\cos\alpha$

Substituting this into the expression for $p$

$p = |\sin\alpha - (-\cos\alpha)| = |\sin\alpha + \cos\alpha|$

The maximum value of the expression $a\sin\alpha + b\cos\alpha$ is $\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}

Here, $a = 1$ and $b = 1$

Maximum value of \sin\alpha + \cos\alpha = \sqrt{1^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{2}$

Therefore, the maximum value of $p$ is $\sqrt{2}

Answer: \sqrt{2}$

84864.subject: Zoology
84864.text: Ten E. coli cells with $N 15$-dsDNA are incubated in medium containing $N 14$ nucleotide. After $60$ minutes, how many E. coli cells will have DNA totally free from $N 15$?
84864.sol:
E. coli has a doubling time of 20 minutes. Thus, in 60 minutes, there would be 3 cycles of doubling. That means, after 60 minutes, there would be 80 E. coli cells, if we start from 10 initial cells.

In the first cycle, all 20 cells would be hybrid DNA containing ${N}^{15} / {N}^{14}state$. The second cycle would yield some 40 cells and out of those, 20 cells would be totally free from ${N}^{15}$ DNA. In the last cycle, there would be 80 cells created and 60 would have ${N}^{14} / {N}^{14}$ state and only 20 cells would have ${N}^{15} / {N}^{14}state$.

So, $- 3 < \dfrac{x^{2} + mx + 1}{x^{2} + x + 1} < 3$
$⇒ - 3 \left(x^{2} + x + 1\right) < x^{2} + mx + 1 < 3\left(x^{2} + x + 1\right)$
$⇒ 4x^{2} + \left(m + 3\right)x + 4 > 0$ and $2x^{2} + \left(3 - m\right)x + 2 > 0$ for real x
$⇒ {\left(m + 3\right)}^{2} - 4 \times 4 \times 4 < 0$ and ${\left(3 - m\right)}^{2} - 4 \times 2 \times 2 < 0$
$⇒ \left(m + 3 + 8\right)\left(m + 3 - 8\right) < 0$ and $\left(m - 3 + 4\right)\left(m - 3 - 4\right) <$0$
$⇒ $\left(m + 11\right)\left(m - 5\right) <$0 and $\left(m + 1\right)\left(m - 7\right) < 0$
$⇒ - 11 < m < 5 and - 1 < m < 7$
Hence, $- 1 < m < 5$

91463.text: The angle between the tangents drawn from the point $\left(4, 1\right)$ to the parabola $x^{2} = 4y$ is
91463.sol:
Equation of the tangent to the parabola $x^{2} = 4y$ having slope $m$ is $x = \dfrac{y}{m} + m$
This tangent passes through $\left(4, 1\right) .$ So,
$4 = m + \dfrac{1}{m}$ or $m^{2} - 4m + 1 = 0$
Now, angle between the tangents is given by
$tan ⁡ \theta = \left|\dfrac{{m}_{1} - {m}_{2}}{1 + {m}_{1}{m}_{2}}\right|$
$= \dfrac{\sqrt{{\left({m}_{1} + {m}_{2}\right)}^{2} - 4{m}_{1}{m}_{2}}}{1 + {m}_{1}{m}_{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{16 - 4}}{1 + 1} = \sqrt{3}$
or $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

92527.text: An $H$-atom moving with speed $v$ makes a head-on collision with another $H$-atom at rest. Both the atoms are in the ground state. The minimum value of velocity $v$ for which one of the atoms may excite is
92527.sol:
For ${v}_\min$ collision should be completely inelastic.

According to energy conservation principle,

$∴ \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_\min^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + ∆ E$ ...(i))

According to momentum conservation principle.

$m{v}_\min = mv + mv$

$∴ v = \dfrac{{m}_\min}{2}$ ...(ii)

After solving eq. (i) an d(ii), we get

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_\min^{2} = 2 ∆ E$

$∴ {v}_\min = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{4 ∆ E}{m}\right)}$

Here, $∆ E =$ minimum excitation energy

$= 10.2eV$

$m = 1.67 \times {10}^{- 27}kg$

$∴ {v}_\min = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{4 \times 10.2 \times 1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}}{1.67 \times {10}^{- 27}}\right)}$

$= \text{6.25} \times {10}^{4}ms^{- 1}$

92688.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
92688.text: A body of mass $2m$ moving with velocity $v$ makes a head-on elastic collision with another body of mass $m$ which is initially at rest. Loss of kinetic energy of the colliding body (mass $2m$) is
92688.sol:
Initial $K . E$ of ball of mass $2m = {K}_{1}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2m \times {v}^{2}$

$= m{v}^{2}$

Collision is elastic so both $K . E$ and momentum are conserved. Let velocities of balls are ${v}_{1} and {v}_{2}$ after collision.



So, $KE$ is conserved

$\dfrac{1}{2}\left(2m\right){v}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2m\right){v}_{1}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{2}^{2}$

$⇒ {v}^{2} = {v}_{1}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}{v}_{2}^{2}$ 

$2( {v}^{2} - {v}_{1}^{2} ) = {v}_{2}^{2} ....( i )$

And, momentum is conserved

$\left(2m\right)v + m\left(0\right) = 2m\left({v}_{1}\right) + m{v}_{2}$

$⇒ 2v = 2{v}_{1} + {v}_{2}$ ... (ii)

Now,

${v}_{2} = 2\left(v - {v}_{1}\right)$

From (i)

$\dfrac{2( {v}^{2} - {v}_{1}^{2} )}{2( v - {v}_{1} )} = \dfrac{{v}_{2}^{2}}{{v}_{2}}$

$v + {v}_{1} = {v}_{2}$

$v - {v}_{1} = \dfrac{{v}_{2}}{2}$

$2{v}_{1} = \dfrac{{v}_{2}}{2}$

${v}_{1} = \dfrac{{v}_{2}}{4} = \dfrac{v}{3}$

So, final $K . E$ of ball of mass $2m$ ,

${k}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(2m\right)\left({v}_{1}^{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2m \times \dfrac{{v}^{2}}{9} = \dfrac{1}{9}\left({k}_{1}\right)$

Hence, loss of $K . E . of {I}^{st}$ ball

$= {K}_{1} - \dfrac{1}{9}{K$}_{1} = $\dfrac{8}{9}{K}_{1}$

100519.subject: Physics
100519.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A particle executing uniform circular motion possesses a constant linear acceleration.
Reason (R): In uniform circular motion, the acceleration vector always points towards the center of the circular path, meaning its direction continuously changes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is not correct
Assertion (A) is not correct but Reason (R) is correct
100519.sol:
In uniform circular motion, the speed of the particle is constant, but its direction of motion changes continuously. The linear acceleration (centripetal acceleration) is directed towards the center of the circular path. As the particle moves along the circle, the direction towards the center continuously changes in space. Since acceleration is a vector quantity, a change in its direction means the acceleration is varying, not constant. Therefore, Assertion (A) is not correct.

Reason (R) correctly states that the acceleration vector points towards the center and its direction continuously changes, which is a true statement.

Answer: Assertion (A) is not correct but Reason (R) is correct

101696.subject: Physics
101696.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When two solid spheres of the same material but radii $r$ and $2r$ fall in a viscous liquid, the viscous drag force on the larger sphere at terminal velocity is 8 times that on the smaller sphere.

Reason (R): The viscous drag force on a sphere at terminal velocity is directly proportional to the cube of its radius.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is not correct
Assertion (A) is not correct but Reason (R) is correct
101696.sol:
At terminal velocity, the net force on the falling sphere is zero. The viscous drag force ($F_v$) exactly balances the effective weight of the sphere (actual weight minus buoyant force).

$F_v = W - F_B$
$F_v = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \sigma g - \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \rho g$
$F_v = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 (\sigma - \rho) g$

For a given material (constant $\sigma$) and liquid (constant $\rho$), the viscous drag force at terminal velocity is directly proportional to the volume of the sphere, and hence to the cube of its radius ($F_v \propto r^3$).

Therefore, Reason (R) is correct.

Using this proportionality for spheres of radii $r$ and $2r$:
$\dfrac{F_{v2}}{F_{v1}} = \left(\dfrac{2r}{r}\right)^3 = 8$

The drag force on the larger sphere is 8 times that on the smaller sphere. Thus, Assertion (A) is correct.

Since Reason (R) provides the exact mathematical relationship used to derive Assertion (A), it is the correct explanation.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

102264.text: Two chambers containing $m_1 \mathrm{~g}$ and $m_2 \mathrm{~g}$ of a gas at pressures $P_1$ and $P_2$ respectively are put in communication with each other, temperature remaining constant. The common pressure reached will be
102264.sol:
According to Boyle'slaw, $P V=k$ (a constant)
or $P \frac{m}{\rho}=k$ or $\rho=\frac{P m}{k}$
$\left(\because V=\frac{m}{\rho}\right)$
$\rho=\frac{P}{K}$
$\left(\because \frac{k}{m}=K\right.$ a constant $)$
So, $\rho_1=\frac{P_1}{K}$ and $V_1=\frac{m_1}{\rho_1}=\frac{m_1}{P_1 / K}=\frac{K m_1}{P_1}$
Similarly, $V_2=\frac{K m_2}{P_2}$
$\therefore \quad$ Total volume $=V_1+V_2=K\left(\frac{m_1}{P_1}+\frac{m_2}{P_2}\right)$
Let $P$ be the common pressure and $\rho$ be the common density of mixture. Then
$\begin{aligned} & \rho=\frac{m_1+m_2}{V_1+V_2}=\frac{m_1+m_2}{K\left(\frac{m_1}{P_1}+\frac{m_2}{P_2}\right)} \\ \therefore \quad P & =K \rho=\frac{m_1+m_2}{\frac{m_1}{P_1}+\frac{m_2}{P_2}}=\frac{P_1 P_2\left(m_1+m_2\right)}{\left(m_1 P_2+m_2 P_1\right)}\end{aligned}$

104707.subject: Physics
104707.text: A beam of unpolarized light is incident on the surface of a transparent medium. It is observed that the reflected light is completely plane-polarized when the angle of incidence is $60^{\circ}$. The angle of refraction in the medium is:
104707.sol:
When unpolarized light is incident at the polarizing angle (Brewster's angle), the reflected light is completely plane-polarized.

According to Brewster's law, at the polarizing angle $i_p$, the reflected and refracted rays are mutually perpendicular.

Therefore, $i_p + r = 90^{\circ}$, where $r$ is the angle of refraction.

Given $i_p = 60^{\circ}$, we have:
$60^{\circ} + r = 90^{\circ}$
$\Rightarrow r = 30^{\circ}$

Answer: $30^{\circ}$

105591.subject: Physics
105591.text: The de-Broglie wavelength of a thermal neutron at $27^{\circ}\text{C}$ is $\lambda_1$. At a temperature of $927^{\circ}\text{C}$, the de-Broglie wavelength of a thermal neutron is $\lambda_2$. The ratio $\lambda_1 : \lambda_2$ is:
105591.sol:
The kinetic energy of a thermal neutron at absolute temperature $T$ is given by $K = \dfrac{3}{2}kT$.

The de-Broglie wavelength is $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{3mkT}}$.

This implies that $\lambda \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{T}}$.

Converting the given temperatures to Kelvin:
$T_1 = 27^{\circ}\text{C} + 273 = 300\text{ K}$
$T_2 = 927^{\circ}\text{C} + 273 = 1200\text{ K}$

Taking the ratio of the wavelengths:
$\dfrac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1200}{300}} = \sqrt{4} = 2$

Thus, the ratio $\lambda_1 : \lambda_2$ is $2 : 1$.

Answer: $2 : 1$

107763.subject: Chemistry
107763.text: According to molecular orbital theory, which of the following diatomic molecules does not exist?
107763.sol:
Total number of electrons in $\text{Be}_2$ is 8.

Its molecular orbital electronic configuration is $\sigma 1s^2 \sigma^{*} 1s^2 \sigma 2s^2 \sigma^{*} 2s^2$.

Here, the number of bonding electrons ($N_b$) = 4 and the number of antibonding electrons ($N_a$) = 4.

Bond order = $\dfrac{1}{2} [N_b - N_a] = \dfrac{1}{2} [4 - 4] = 0$.

Since the bond order is zero, the $\text{Be}_2$ molecule does not exist.

$\text{Li}_2$ (6 electrons), $\text{B}_2$ (10 electrons), and $\text{C}_2$ (12 electrons) have bond orders of 1, 1, and 2 respectively, so they are stable and exist.

Answer: $\text{Be}_2$

114380.subject: Chemistry
114380.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If the standard electrode potentials for $A^{2+}/A$ and $A^+/A$ are $x$ V and $y$ V respectively, then the standard electrode potential for $A^{2+}/A^+$ is $(2x - y)$ V.
Reason (R): Standard electrode potentials are extensive properties and can be directly added or subtracted to obtain the potential of a new half-cell.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct
114380.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct: The standard electrode potentials cannot be directly added, but standard Gibbs free energy changes ($\Delta G^\circ$) can be.
For $A^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow A$, $\Delta G^\circ_1 = -2Fx$
For $A^+ + e^- \rightarrow A$, $\Delta G^\circ_2 = -Fy$
The target reaction is $A^{2+} + e^- \rightarrow A^+$, which is obtained by subtracting the second reaction from the first.
$\Delta G^\circ_3 = \Delta G^\circ_1 - \Delta G^\circ_2 = -2Fx - (-Fy) = -2Fx + Fy$
Since $\Delta G^\circ_3 = -1FE^\circ_3$, we have $-FE^\circ_3 = -F(2x - y)$, which gives $E^\circ_3 = (2x - y)$ V.

Reason (R) is incorrect: Standard electrode potential ($E^\circ$) is an intensive property, meaning it does not depend on the amount of substance. Because it is an intensive property, electrode potentials cannot be directly added or subtracted. Instead, the extensive property $\Delta G^\circ$ must be used for such calculations.

Answer: Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect

119279.subject: Chemistry
119279.text:
2-Butanone reacts with hydrogen cyanide to form an intermediate P. The intermediate P is then heated strongly with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to form a major product Q.

Identify the IUPAC name of the major product Q.
119279.sol:
2-Butanone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) undergoes nucleophilic addition with $\text{HCN}$ to form a cyanohydrin intermediate P, which is 2-hydroxy-2-methylbutanenitrile.

When this cyanohydrin is heated strongly with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, two reactions occur: the nitrile group ($-\text{CN}$) is hydrolyzed to a carboxylic acid group ($-\text{COOH}$), and the hydroxyl group ($-\text{OH}$) undergoes acid-catalyzed dehydration.

Dehydration follows Saytzeff's rule, where hydrogen is eliminated from the adjacent carbon with fewer hydrogen atoms to yield the more substituted, more stable alkene. Thus, hydrogen is lost from the $-\text{CH}_2-$ group rather than the $-\text{CH}_3$ group.

The resulting major product Q is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{COOH}$, which is named 2-methylbut-2-enoic acid.

Answer: 2-Methylbut-2-enoic acid

119298.subject: Chemistry
119298.text: What is the major product formed when butanoyl chloride undergoes hydrogenation in the presence of palladium supported on barium sulfate?
119298.sol:
The reaction of an acyl chloride with hydrogen gas in the presence of palladium supported on barium sulfate (Pd-BaSO4) is known as the Rosenmund reduction.

In this reaction, the acyl chloride is reduced to the corresponding aldehyde. Barium sulfate acts as a catalytic poison, preventing further reduction of the aldehyde to an alcohol.

Therefore, butanoyl chloride is reduced to butanal.

Answer: Butanal

123441.subject: Botany
123441.text: During secondary growth in dicot stems, the formation of phelloderm from phellogen is an example of which of the following developmental processes?
123441.sol:
Phellogen (cork cambium) is a secondary meristem formed by the process of dedifferentiation. When the cells of phellogen divide and the newly formed cells mature to form phelloderm (secondary cortex), they lose their capacity to divide.

According to NCERT, the process by which the derivatives of a dedifferentiated tissue lose their ability to divide and mature to perform specific functions is called redifferentiation.

Dedifferentiation is incorrect because it refers to the formation of the phellogen itself, not its products. Differentiation applies to primary tissues, and plasticity refers to different pathways in response to environment or phases of life.

Answer: Redifferentiation

123555.text: What is the average duration of cell cycle of a human cell?
123555.sol: A typical eukaryotic cell cycle is illustrated by human cells in culture. These cells divide once in approximately every 24 hours. However, this duration of cell cycle can vary from organism to organism and also from cell type to cell type. Yeast for example, can progress through the cell cycle in only about 90 minutes. The cell cycle is divided into two basic phases: Interphase, M Phase (Mitosis phase) The M Phase represents the phase when the actual cell division or mitosis occurs and the interphase represents the phase between two successive M phases.

Electron micrographs of this stage indicate that chromosome synapsis is accompanied by the formation of complex structure called synaptonemal complex. The complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called a bivalent or a tetrad. however, these are more clearly visible at the next stage. The first two stages of prophase I are relatively short-lived compared to the next stage that is pachytene.

124323.subject: Botany
124323.text:
Read the following statements regarding the formulation of the cell theory:

(I) Matthias Schleiden, a German zoologist, examined a large number of plants and observed that all plants are composed of different kinds of cells.
(II) Theodore Schwann studied different types of animal cells and reported that cells had a thin outer layer.
(III) Schwann also concluded, based on his studies on plant tissues, that the presence of cell wall is a unique character of the plant cells.
(IV) Rudolf Virchow explained that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells.

How many of the above statements are correct?
124323.sol:
Statement (I) is incorrect because Matthias Schleiden was a German botanist, not a zoologist.

Statement (II) is correct. Theodore Schwann (1839), a British zoologist, reported the presence of a thin outer layer (plasma membrane) in animal cells.

Statement (III) is correct. Despite being a zoologist, Schwann studied plant tissues and concluded that the cell wall is a unique character of plant cells.

Statement (IV) is correct. Rudolf Virchow (1855) modified the hypothesis of Schleiden and Schwann to give the cell theory a final shape by explaining that new cells arise from pre-existing cells.

Thus, exactly three statements (II, III, and IV) are correct.

Answer: Only three

124977.subject: Botany
124977.text: How many molecules of CO2 are produced from the complete oxidation of pyruvate?
124977.sol:
For aerobic respiration to take place within the mitochondria, the final product of glycolysis, pyruvate is transported from the cytoplasm into the mitochondria. The crucial events in aerobic respiration are:

• The complete oxidation of pyruvate by the stepwise removal of all the hydrogen atoms, leaving three molecules of CO2 .

• The passing on of the electrons removed as part of the hydrogen atoms to molecular O2 with simultaneous synthesis of ATP.

What is interesting to note is that the first process takes place in the matrix of the mitochondria while the second process is located on the inner membrane of the mitochondria

125906.subject: Botany
125906.text: What happens when an animal carrying pollen on its body comes into contact with the stigma?
options: It causes the flower to close
It results in the dispersal of seeds
It leads to the production of nectar
125906.sol: Majority of insect-pollinated flowers are large, colourful, fragrant and rich in nectar. When the flowers are small, a number of flowers are clustered into an inflorescence to make them conspicuous. Animals are attracted to flowers by colour and/or fragrance. The flowers pollinated by flies and beetles secrete foul odours to attract these animals. To sustain animal visits, the flowers have to provide rewards to the animals. Nectar and pollen grains are the usual floral rewards. For harvesting the reward(s) from the flower the animal visitor comes in contact with the anthers and the stigma. The body of the animal gets a coating of pollen grains, which are generally sticky in animal pollinated flowers. When the animal carrying pollen on its body comes in contact with the stigma, it brings about pollination.

125932.subject: Botany
125932.text: What should be done if the female parent plant produces unisexual flowers?
options: The flower buds need to be removed from the plant
The flower buds should be bagged before opening, and pollination is carried out when the stigma is receptive
Pollen from the male parent should be applied directly without any bagging
125932.sol: This is achieved by emasculation and bagging techniques. If the female parent bears bisexual flowers, removal of anthers from the flower bud before the anther dehisces using a pair of forceps is necessary. This step is referred to as emasculation. Emasculated flowers have to be covered with a bag of suitable size, generally made up of butter paper, to prevent contamination of its stigma with unwanted pollen. This process is called bagging. When the stigma of bagged flower attains receptivity, mature pollen grains collected from anthers of the male parent are dusted on the stigma, and the flowers are rebagged, and the fruits allowed to develop. If the female parent produces unisexual flowers, there is no need for emasculation. The female flower buds are bagged before the flowers open. When the stigma becomes receptive, pollination is carried out using the desired pollen and the flower rebagged.

126748.subject: Botany
126748.text:
Read the following biomolecule-category pairs carefully:
(A) Uridine - Nitrogenous base
(B) Adenylic acid - Nucleotide
(C) Morphine - Alkaloid
(D) Carotenoids - Pigment
(E) Ricin - Drug

How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
126748.sol:
Let us evaluate each pair based on the classification of biomolecules:
(A) Uridine is a nucleoside (uracil attached to a ribose sugar), not a nitrogenous base. The nitrogenous base itself is uracil. (Incorrect)
(B) Adenylic acid has a phosphate group esterified to the sugar of adenosine, making it a nucleotide. (Correct)
(C) Morphine is classified as an alkaloid. (Correct)
(D) Carotenoids are classified as pigments. (Correct)
(E) Ricin is classified as a toxin, whereas drugs include compounds like vinblastin and curcumin. (Incorrect)

Therefore, exactly three pairs (B, C, and D) are correctly matched.

Answer: Three

127615.text: How many trophic levels are possible in the grazing food chain?
127615.sol: Each trophic level has a certain mass of living material at a particular time called as the standing crop. The standing crop is measured as the mass of living organisms (biomass) or the number in a unit area. The biomass of a species is expressed in terms of fresh or dry weight. Measurement of biomass in terms of dry weight is more accurate. Why?The number of trophic levels in the grazing food chain is restricted as the transfer of energy follows 10 per cent law – only 10 per cent of the energy is transferred to each trophic level from the lower trophic level. In nature, it is possible to have so many levels – producer, herbivore, primary carnivore, secondary carnivore in the grazing food chain

Match List-I with List-II regarding the anatomy of a cockroach.

B. Malpighian tubulesII. Assists in excretion

128124.sol:
In a cockroach, Hepatic caeca (or gastric caeca) are a ring of 6-8 blind tubules present at the junction of the foregut and midgut, which secrete digestive juice.

Malpighian tubules are a ring of 100-150 yellow-coloured thin filamentous tubules present at the junction of the midgut and hindgut, which help in the removal of excretory products (uric acid).

Gizzard (proventriculus) has an outer layer of thick circular muscles and thick inner cuticle forming six highly chitinous plates called teeth, which help in grinding the food particles.

Fat body, nephrocytes and urecose glands are secondary structures that also assist in excretion.

Answer: A - III, B - IV, C - I, D - II

129696.subject: Zoology
129696.text: A patient experiences a significant increase in blood flow to the atria of the heart due to elevated blood volume. Which of the following correctly describes the immediate hormonal response and its direct physiological consequence?
options: Release of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF), which stimulates the renin-angiotensin mechanism to maintain glomerular filtration rate
Release of Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) from the neurohypophysis to further increase blood volume and pressure
Release of aldosterone from the adrenal cortex to promote the excretion of excess sodium and water
Release of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF), which causes vasodilation and acts as a check on the renin-angiotensin mechanism
129696.sol:
An increase in blood flow to the atria of the heart stimulates the release of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF).

ANF causes vasodilation (dilation of blood vessels) and thereby decreases blood pressure. Furthermore, ANF acts as a check on the renin-angiotensin mechanism, opposing its effects.

Option 1 is incorrect because ANF inhibits, rather than stimulates, the renin-angiotensin mechanism.

Option 2 is incorrect because ADH is released in response to low blood volume or excessive fluid loss, not elevated blood volume.

Option 3 is incorrect because aldosterone promotes the reabsorption of sodium and water, not their excretion.

Answer: Release of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF), which causes vasodilation and acts as a check on the renin-angiotensin mechanism

A fall in glomerular filtration rate (GFR)
129731.sol:
According to NCERT, an increase in body fluid volume switches off the osmoreceptors and suppresses the release of ADH to complete the feedback loop, thereby promoting diuresis.

Excessive loss of fluid from the body activates osmoreceptors, stimulating the hypothalamus to release ADH. Answer: Increase in body fluid volume

Answer: Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.

131837.subject: Zoology
131837.text: During the process of transcription in bacteria, a stage is reached where the nascent RNA falls off and the RNA polymerase also separates from the DNA, marking the end of the process. Which of the following transiently associates with the RNA polymerase to facilitate this specific event?
131837.sol:
In prokaryotes, the core RNA polymerase is only capable of catalysing the elongation step of transcription.

To terminate the process, the RNA polymerase must transiently associate with a termination factor, known as the $\rho$ (rho) factor, when it reaches the terminator region. This association alters the specificity of the enzyme, causing the nascent RNA and the polymerase to fall off the DNA.

The $\sigma$ (sigma) factor is required for initiation, not termination. The core enzyme cannot terminate transcription on its own, and DNA helicase is involved in unwinding DNA during replication, not transcription termination.

Answer: $\rho$ (rho) factor

132266.subject: Zoology
132266.text: What is the likelihood of a heterozygous individual being affected by sickle-cell anaemia?
132266.sol: This is an autosome linked recessive trait that can be transmitted from parents to the offspring when both the partners are carrier for the gene (or heterozygous). The disease is controlled by a single pair of allele, HbA and HbS . Out of the three possible genotypes only homozygous individuals for HbS (HbSHbS ) show the diseased phenotype. Heterozygous (HbAHbS ) individuals appear apparently unaffected but they are carrier of the disease as there is 50 per cent probability of transmission of the mutant gene to the progeny, thus exhibiting sickle-cell trait (Figure 4.15). The defect is caused by the substitution of Glutamic acid) by Valine (Val) at the sixth position of the beta globin chain of the haemoglobin molecule. The substitution of amino acid in the globin protein results due to the single base substitution at the sixth codon of the beta globin gene from GAG to GUG. The mutant haemoglobin molecule undergoes polymerisation under low oxygen tension causing the change in the shape of the RBC from biconcave disc to elongated sickle like structure

133044.subject: Zoology
133044.text: When two species of different genealogy come to resemble each other as a result of adaptation, the phenomenon is termed:
133044.sol:
The analogous organs show convergent evolution due to similar adaptions which do not support organic evolution. Divergent evolution occurs when two groups of the same species evolve different traits within those groups in order to accommodate for differing environmental and social pressures. Microevolution is the change in allele frequencies that occurs over a relatively short period of time within a population. This change is due to four different processes: mutation, selection, gene flow and genetic drift. Coevolution refers to the evolution of at least two species, which occurs in a mutually dependent manner.
Related Theory
As bat's wing and bird's wing have similar structure and origin i.e., they have bony structures hence, they are called homologous organs, showing divergent evolution. Bat's wing is analogous to the wing of an insect, because the wing of an insect does not have a bony structure, it has membranous wing. So bat's wing and insect's wing are analogous showing convergent evolution, because they have similar functions but do not have the same origin and structure.

133375.subject: Zoology
133375.text:
Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion: The most important measure to control diseases like malaria and filariasis is to administer vaccines.
Reason: Controlling or eliminating insect vectors and their breeding places is crucial for preventing diseases like malaria and filariasis.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Assertion is false, but Reason is true
133375.sol: For diseases such as malaria and filariasis that are transmitted through insect vectors, the most important measure is to control or eliminate the vectors and their breeding places. This can be achieved by avoiding stagnation of water in and around residential areas, regular cleaning of household coolers, use of mosquito nets, introducing fishes like Gambusia in ponds that feed on mosquito larvae, spraying of insecticides in ditches, drainage areas and swamps, etc. In addition, doors and windows should be provided with wire mesh to prevent the entry of mosquitoes. Such precautions have become more important especially in the light of recent widespread incidences of the vector-borne (Aedes mosquitoes) diseases like dengue and chikungunya in many parts of India. The advancements made in biological science have armed us to effectively deal with many infectious diseases. The use of vaccines and immunisation programmes have enabled us to completely eradicate a deadly disease like smallpox. A large number of other infectious diseases like polio, diphtheria, pneumonia and tetanus have been controlled to a large extent by the use of vaccines. Biotechnology (about which you will read more in Chapter 10) is at the verge of making available newer and safer vaccines. Discovery of antibiotics and various other drugs has also enabled us to effectively treat infectious diseases.
